market_view: The S&P 500 (7,811.54, +0.59% Fri Oct 9) sits near its record after a volatile week. Monday is a thin Columbus Day session with bonds closed, and the 10-year yield is around 5.24%, so expect chop until the bank prints Tuesday and CPI Wednesday; AI and semis sentiment is still fragile after the OpenAI revenue scare.
lessons: Moonshots bought after an after-hours reaction to news everyone had already seen gave back the gap: CLOV (+4-7% AH on 5-star ratings) fell 7.2% and NN fell 5% the next session. Buying an opening gap on overnight news has had negative edge, so these get low confidence and wide stops at most.

Analyst initiations alone were not moonshot catalysts on beaten-down names: KTOS (Barclays $90 target) fell 1.6% and RKLB fell 0.9%. PLTR worked (+3.8%) because two Street calls hit a stock already showing relative strength at a record.

Pre-print run-ups on cost-squeezed names fail: DAL stopped out at -5% when fuel up 62% y/y drove a miss and guide cut. By contrast CCI (+7%), a direct second-order beneficiary of the SpaceX spectrum deal, worked, so fresh structural news beats generic pre-earnings positioning.

Rebounded 2.4% Friday to $535.07 with no negative news; thesis intact into late-October earnings.
Up 3.3% Friday on Prime Big Deal Days checks and AWS commentary; the WSJ-reported ~$7B Decart talks are immaterial to the thesis.

moonshot.thesis: Bloomberg/Reuters reported after Friday's close (Oct 9) that GTCR and Elliott are in advanced talks to take CCC private, with a deal possible as soon as this week. Shares closed $7.02 and traded $7.99 after hours, and a signed deal at a premium would push them toward the take-out price.
moonshot.catalyst_time: 2026-10-09 after close (report); definitive agreement possible 2026-10-12 onward
moonshot.main_risk: The ~14% after-hours gap already prices much of a premium, and with no price or signed agreement the open could fade like CLOV/NN did. Talks collapsing invalidates the thesis.

moonshot.thesis: Mirum announced Sunday (Oct 11) that it will release topline Phase 3 EXPAND results for LIVMARLI in ultra-rare cholestatic liver diseases Monday morning with an 8:30am ET call. A positive label-expansion readout on an already-marketed drug can extend Friday's 5.7% gain intraday.
moonshot.main_risk: Binary: results aren't public yet. A miss or mixed data on secondary endpoints gaps it down, and even good data may be bought at an already-gapped open.

moonshot.thesis: First Tracks announced Sunday (Oct 11) Phase 1b cohort 1 topline data for CD122 antagonist ANB033 in celiac disease (gluten challenge) Monday morning with an 8:30am webcast. A clean protective signal in celiac, an indication with no approved drug, could re-rate the ~$1.1B company.
moonshot.main_risk: Small early cohort and a history of celiac failures. An ambiguous signal or a sell-the-news reaction after the stock held ~$32 would break it.

moonshot.thesis: Freenome released improved validation data for its next-gen colorectal cancer blood test Sunday at 1pm ET (Oct 11): 80.4% cancer sensitivity at 90% specificity, and advanced precancerous lesion sensitivity up to 18.2% from 13.7%, ahead of an ACG late-breaker Oct 14. First regular session to react is Monday.
moonshot.main_risk: The improvement is incremental and competitors' tests set a high bar. A 75M-share resale registration from the July IPO is an overhang on any pop.

moonshot.thesis: Goldman's Oct 8 upgrade to Buy ($230) and Barclays' Oct 9 Overweight initiation ($265) pushed PLTR to a record close of $209.05 (+5.2%) while software rebounded. Breakouts with fresh Street support and relative strength have followed through, and my PLTR moonshot last session made +3.8%.
moonshot.main_risk: At ~110x forward earnings, any renewed AI-revenue scare (like Thursday's OpenAI report) reverses it, and Monday's thin holiday tape may not carry momentum.

catalyst.thesis: Humana's Oct 8 release says 95% of members are now in 4+ star 2027 Medicare Advantage plans (vs 20% for 2026), a large 2028 bonus tailwind, and it reaffirmed 2026 EPS of at least $9. Baird upgraded to Outperform ($596 target) and Barclays raised to $582 on Oct 9, so estimates should keep rising. The stock closed $431.87 (+11.6%) and held $435 after hours.
catalyst.catalyst_time: 2026-10-08 star ratings; 2026-10-09 upgrades; estimate revisions 2026-10-12 to 10-14
catalyst.main_risk: It faded 5% from the $456.50 high Friday and is up ~63% YTD; Baird notes profits depend on how much is reinvested in benefits. A CMS ratings dispute or a rotation out of managed care breaks it.

catalyst.thesis: Morgan Stanley double-upgraded Cboe to Overweight on Oct 9 (target $358 from $258), citing durable options growth after the Sep 29 extension of its exclusive S&P index license through 2051. It trades at ~17.6x 2027 EPS vs a 22x 3-year average and ~18% under its $371 high, so institutions have room to re-rate it.
catalyst.main_risk: Already up ~8% in two days. Falling volatility (VIX 14.8) could cool option volumes; earnings aren't until Oct 30.

catalyst.thesis: The FDA approved Weltruza on Oct 9, the first once-monthly subcutaneous olanzapine injection for schizophrenia, with a US launch in the coming weeks. TEVA rose 4.7% to $41.10 on ~14M shares, nearly 3x average volume, at a 52-week high, and estimate and target updates should follow this week.
catalyst.main_risk: The approval was largely expected, peak-sales guidance isn't given, and the stock is extended at its high with a ~65x trailing P/E.

catalyst.thesis: ASML reports Q3 Wed Oct 14 before the open, and the 3-session hold covers the print. It guided Q3 sales to EUR11-12B (vs EUR9.33B in Q2) and raised FY26 to EUR43-45B, while TSMC's record Q3 revenue (above guidance) confirms leading-edge demand. The stock fell ~4.7% last week in the AI scare to $1,780, ~10% under its high.
catalyst.main_risk: At ~55x trailing, soft EUV/High-NA orders or cautious 2027 commentary get punished, and it is correlated with my TSM position and semis sentiment.

catalyst.thesis: Goldman reports Q3 Tue Oct 13 before the open after falling in 10 of 12 weeks to $895, 22% below its $1,154 high and under both 200-day ($987) and 50-day averages, at ~14x trailing. Consensus has been cut to ~$15.2-15.4 EPS (vs a record $20.98 in Q2), and heavy Q3-end M&A and record equity markets set up a low bar.
catalyst.main_risk: Management flagged softer fixed-income trading, and with yields at 5.2% bank sentiment is poor. It also stacks on my JPM and WFC print exposure the same morning.
